headline: Clifford Bennett cautious on Bitcoin short-term, tightening take-profit stops after strong run
reasoning: Bennett acknowledges Bitcoin has benefited from the same US deficit and US asset concern narrative that has driven gold higher, as investors seek alternatives. However, he believes Bitcoin is due for a downward correction after a significant recent run. He is tightening take-profit stops considerably, signalling a more cautious near-term posture rather than outright bearishness.
quote: One of the reasons Bitcoin has benefited too, is that the, you know, the deficit in the US, etc. is triggering concerns about US assets in general. And so people have gone to the alternative. Again, there are other factors at play, but that's something to keep an eye on as well. Bitcoin's due for a downward correction. We've just had a great run in it and we're tightening up. Our take profit stops up quite a bit.
episode_title: Why Clifford is still bullish on oil and gold

headline: Clifford Bennett remains bullish on oil over 1-2 year horizon, sees any near-term softness as a buying opportunity
reasoning: Bennett believes oil is currently fairly priced, having already priced in significant risk of a larger Middle East conflict. He expects short-term softness as the market pivots to a narrative that US economic warfare means stable or higher oil supply, allowing attention to shift back to AI and tech. However, he argues the world remains approximately 10% short of normal oil supply, and that it will take 1-2 years for supply to return to normal levels. While other global producers are increasing output to offset Middle East disruption, they cannot fully compensate. He views any pullback as a dip-buying opportunity with a long-term bullish outlook.
quote: I do think that, um, yeah, I think gold and oil both are still a buy. I think oil softens a little bit here. We've seen a little bit today, but it could soften for several days. On the idea that the US has moved to economic warfare. So therefore we're going to get the same or higher levels of oil supply... If oil consolidates here pulls back I think it's a buy on the dip because it is going to be 1 to 2 years before oil supply returns to normal. It is also on the other side of the ledger, the case that other other producers of oil around the world are increasing production to offset the Middle East, but they can't do that fully. So I think the world is still 10% short on normal oil supply.
episode_title: Why Clifford is still bullish on oil and gold

headline: Clifford Bennett warns geopolitical risk in the Middle East is being underestimated by markets, sees risk of broader conflict post-US midterms
reasoning: Bennett argues that the current Middle East conflict has already inflicted serious costs on the US, including the destruction of its largest naval base in the region. He believes the US may see the midterms as a reset and could pursue a more aggressive military posture if Congressional seats are maintained, raising the risk of an escalated conflict. A worst-case scenario would see destruction of oil and energy infrastructure, including desalination plants, creating a global crisis. He urges investors to factor this tail risk into their portfolios.
quote: The world is against the war. It's not a popular war at home or abroad, and it is proving very costly militarily for the US, particularly in bases. You know, their largest naval base in the Middle East has been completely destroyed and put out of commission and may never be rebuilt... I have a feeling, a sad feeling that after the midterms they will feel they have a clean slate if they've maintained the vote in the House... So I hope the war is over. But people are underestimating the risks... The risk is another war like we just saw. It's a much more significant and larger war that destroys all oil infrastructure, energy infrastructure, perhaps even desalinization plants Across the Middle East, it becomes a global crisis worse than we've so far seen.
episode_title: Why Clifford is still bullish on oil and gold

headline: Clifford Bennett calls gold a great long-term buy, sees multi-year bull market underway driven by US deficit concerns
reasoning: Bennett states he flagged gold's readiness for another multi-year bull market before the recent rally started. He notes the rally in gold is now steady and sustained rather than spectacular like earlier 2025 surges. A key driver is concern over the US fiscal deficit triggering broader anxiety about US assets, pushing investors toward alternative stores of value including gold. He acknowledges there will be volatility and downside zags along the way but maintains a high-conviction long-term bullish stance on gold.
quote: For gold, gold just keeps climbing because I think gold has actually started in the last few weeks. And I did say this before this rally started, that it was ready for another multi-year bull market in gold. Now, it won't be as spectacular as the previous, uh, rallies we saw at the start of the year. But it will be a steady climb and there will be zags as well. To the downside, there will be volatility. But I think gold still and you know it was definitely a few weeks ago a great long term buy. But I do think gold is still a great long term buy.
episode_title: Why Clifford is still bullish on oil and gold
